findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: the slope of the 2-day return minus drift on the forecast is +0.00039 with a day-clustered t of 1.81 (8,650 grid bars, 4,217 with a positive forecast over 1,125 days), and the top fifth of positive forecasts beats the drift by +0.73 % (t 1.69, 844 cases on 297 days), so the effect points the predicted way but is too small for six coins to show clearly.
findings.F2: The effect is spread across most coins, not confined to one. At 2 days the slope is positive on 4 of 6 coins: XRP t 2.43, LTC 1.86, ZEC 1.59 and XMR 1.57, while BTC (t -0.32) and ETH (t -0.02) are flat. It is also positive in 7 of 8 years, each year's t below 1.2, with 2022 the one negative year (t -0.72). This is a small, broad effect that more coins and days would sharpen, not one living in a single part of the data.
findings.F3: The effect is clearest at the 1-day horizon and fades as the horizon lengthens: the slope's t is 3.57 at 1 day (17,380 cases), 1.81 at 2 days, 1.04 at 3, -0.11 at 5 and 1.05 at 10.
findings.F4: At 1 day, all 6 coins have a positive slope (XMR t 5.04, XRP 3.27, LTC 2.32, ZEC 2.30, ETH 1.85, BTC 1.49), and 7 of 8 years are positive (2025 is -0.32).
findings.F5: The rebound is graded with the size of the fall measured in the coin's own 60-day standard deviations. At 1 day the move beyond drift rises from -0.04 % after falls of 0 to 0.5 sd, to +0.26 % after 0.5 to 1 sd, +0.65 % after 1.5 to 2 sd, +0.85 % after 2 to 3 sd (t 2.03, 259 cases), and +2.35 % after falls above 3 sd (75 cases).
findings.F6: The plan's forecast standardises the scaled fall against its own past 61 values, which blurs the grading: its lower three positive quintiles at 2 days sit below drift (-0.13 %, -0.37 %, -0.29 %). The raw scaled fall that the idea names gives a slope t of 2.23 at 2 days and 2.61 at 1 day.
findings.F7: The pooled unusual move per case (+0.15 %, t 0.86) is 0.8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The top-fifth forecasts carry +0.69 % at 1 day and +0.73 % at 2 days beyond drift, several times the cost. So the trade is worth taking only on the most unusual falls, and only if the effect holds on more data.

ideas.name: unusual falls rebound, more coins
ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, measured against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: A dip buyer should size the bet by how unusual the fall is for the coin's recent volatility, not by how volatile the coin has been, since only the falls that are most unusual for the coin pay well beyond the cost of a trade.
